claim_verdicts.evidence: Recording rules page: recording rules "allow you to precompute frequently needed or computationally expensive expressions and save their result as a new set of time series"; record: "The name of the time series to output to. Must be a valid metric name."; expr: "The PromQL expression to evaluate." Versioned 3.5 URL returned 404; /latest/ page used.
Configuration page: "Rule files specifies a list of globs. Rules and alerts are read from all matching files." prometheus.yaml@stage-4 line 55 uses the glob /etc/prometheus/rules/*.yml.

Recording rules page: "Rules within a group are run sequentially at a regular interval, with the same evaluation time." Group interval: "[ interval: <duration> | default = global.evaluation_interval ]".

Operators page: "`by` does the opposite and drops labels that are not listed in the `by` clause"; "In any arithmetic binary operation involving vectors, the metric name is dropped." Recording rules page, labels: "Labels to add or overwrite before storing the result." The slo.rules.yml rules set no labels, so the result carries only job.

Recording rules page: rules in a group "are run sequentially at a regular interval"; nothing ties evaluation to queries. Global: "[ evaluation_interval: <duration> | default = 1m ]", staging sets 15s (prometheus.yaml@stage-4 line 53).

Recording rules page: Prometheus precomputes expressions and "save[s] their result as a new set of time series" in its own storage. Nothing in the api changes: DonHang.Api /metrics is produced by prometheus-net, untouched by the rule file (only config-repo/platform/monitoring changed).
Storage page, Backfilling for Recording Rules: "When a new recording rule is created, there is no historical data for it. Recording rule data only exists from the creation time on."

Round 3: section 4 now says "a volume that lives only as long as its Pod (`emptyDir` in the file)"; still matches. volumes.md (refs) l.163-167: the volume "is created when the Pod is assigned to a node"; "When a Pod is removed from a node for any reason, the data in the emptyDir is deleted permanently." prometheus.yaml@stage-4 l.138-146: a changed rule renames the ConfigMap, "changes this Pod template and restarts Prometheus"; data is emptyDir: {}.

prometheus.yaml@stage-4 (828fdeb): l.49 "scrape_interval: 5s", l.53 "evaluation_interval: 15s", l.55 "- /etc/prometheus/rules/*.yml", l.130-131 mount rules at /etc/prometheus/rules, l.142-144 configMap name slo-rules; kustomization.yaml configMapGenerator slo-rules from rules/slo.rules.yml.

slo.rules.yml@stage-4 l.12-21: group slo-s3-product-reads, four records ratio_rate5m/30m/1h/6h, each 1 - sum by (job)(rate(...code!~"5..")) / sum by (job)(rate(...)). slo.md l.50-52: same method/endpoint/code filters as a good-share ratio of increase over [28d].

prometheus.yaml@stage-4 l.63 "job_name: api", l.69-71 keep regex "api|api-canary|api-green" on __meta_kubernetes_pod_label_app, l.75-76 copy it to label app; Deployments api, api-canary, api-green set Pod label app to their own name. One job, so sum by (job) merges all three.

Best practices, Recording rules: "Recording rules should be of the general form level:metric:operations." "level represents the aggregation level and labels of the rule output." "operations is a list of operations that were applied to the metric, newest operation first." Example names include job:request_failures_per_requests:ratio_rate5m.
Data model page: "Colons (':') are reserved for user-defined recording rules. They SHOULD NOT be used by exporters or direct instrumentation."

slo.rules.yml@stage-4: 16 `record:` lines (l.14-20, 47-53, 75-81, 103-109), level job:. S2/S4 use 1 - bucket{le="0.512"|"2.048"} / _count. Each group's alerts: FastBurn reads ratio_rate1h and ratio_rate5m (l.26, 56, 84, 112), SlowBurn reads ratio_rate6h and ratio_rate30m (l.36, 64, 92, 120).

Conditioned opinion. Recording rules page supports the premise: rules "precompute frequently needed or computationally expensive expressions". The lesson states the condition ("Several alerts and panels read the same share, all the time" vs "A query is run once").
Design choices stated with conditions, derived from the repo (sum by (job) in slo.rules.yml, app label from relabel_configs l.75-76 of prometheus.yaml). No documentation fact asserted.

Round 3. Jobs and instances page: Prometheus attaches labels to scraped series, "`job`: The configured job name that the target belongs to."; if job already exists in the scraped data, "the behavior depends on the `honor_labels` configuration option" (not set here). prometheus.yaml@stage-4 l.63 "- job_name: api".

Round 3. Querying basics: "`!~`: Select labels that do not regex-match the provided string." "Regex matches are always fully anchored." slo.md@stage-4 l.26: the two GET product endpoints are api/v1/products and api/v1/products/{id:int}; both fully match api/v1/products.*.
